thread.title: Consumer Sector Update for 01/08/2018: KSS,WHR,HON,AAPL

author: MT Newswires
title: Consumer Sector Update for 01/08/2018: KSS,WHR,HON,AAPL
text:
Shutterstock photo Top Consumer Stocks
WMT +1.43%
MCD -0.06%
DIS -1.44%
CVS -0.77%
KO -0.20%
Consumer stocks were ending slightly higher Monday, with shares of consumer staples companies in the S&P 500 climbing just over 0.2% in late afternoon trading while shares of consumer discretionary firms in the S&P 500 were adding almost 0.1% in value, paring a much larger advance earlier today.
In industry news:
+ Whirlpool ( WHR ) was fractionally higher Monday after the appliance manufacturer said it will be collaborating with Honeywell ( HON ) and Apple ( AAPL ) to develop a line of "smart" appliances linked to Honeywell's connected thermostats and allowing consumers to use their iWatches, iPhones and other Apple devices to remotely manage those products as well as adjusting home temperatures. The companies are expecting to introduce more than 20 of the connected Whirlpool appliances during 2018, they said.
Among consumer stocks moving on news:
+ Kohl's ( KSS ) climbed to a new 52-week high on Monday after the department store retailer today reported a combined 6.9% increase in comparable-store sales during November and December, topping internal forecasts. Based on that stronger-than-expected performance, Kohl's also raised its guidance for FY17 adjusted earnings to a new range of $3.98 to $4.08, up from $3.60 to $3.80 per share previously and topping the Capital IQ consensus by at least $0.22 per share.
In other sector news:
+ Crocs ( CROX ) raced to a 28-month high on Monday after updating its Q4 outlook, projecting between $195 mln to $198 mln in sales, up from its prior range expecting $180 mln to $190 mln and beating the Capital IQ consensus by at least $8.3 mln. It also reiterated its online FY17 sales guidance.
+ Stage Stores (SSI) advanced Monday after narrowing its projected FY17 net loss to a new range of $0.90 to $1.15 per share after reporting a 1.1% increase in comparable-store sales during the nine weeks ended Dec. 30. The company previously was expecting as large as a $1.25 per share net loss.
+ Darden Restaurants (DRI) was rising after the restaurant chain raised its FY18 non-GAAP profit outlook to a new range of $4.70 to $4.78 per share compared with its prior view expecting between $4.45 to $4.53 per share.
